hook_clip: Here's what PandaDoc really costs a small team, and when you don't need it. Ten seats on the Business plan come to five thousand eight hundred and eighty dollars a year.
outro_clip: The full spec is free at personal software factory dot com. If you build it, tell me what broke. I'm Sam. See you tomorrow.

scenes.text: PandaDoc publishes two plans for small teams. Starter is nineteen dollars per seat per month, and allows up to five templates. Business is forty-nine dollars per seat per month, with unlimited templates. Those prices are from PandaDoc's own pricing page, checked in October twenty twenty-six.

Both plans are priced per seat, so the bill grows with the team. For ten people, Starter comes to two thousand two hundred and eighty dollars a year. And every extra person on Business adds five hundred and eighty-eight dollars a year.

The limit that pushes small teams up a tier is templates. Starter stops at five. If you send more than five kinds of quote, you're on Business. A similar tool, Proposify, puts discount approvals on its Grow plan, at three hundred and twenty-five dollars a month for five seats.
But what does a small team actually use? Often it's one job. Price a few line items for a client from a price list. Apply a discount within the rules. And get a yes.

So buy PandaDoc if you need legally binding e-signatures, payment collection, CRM sync, or a drag-and-drop document designer. Build it if your team sends quotes from a known price list, and a typed-name acceptance is enough for your deals.

That's what our Quote Builder blueprint covers. Line items, discounts, tax and live totals. A manager approval for any discount over the limit. And a client link to accept or decline. Claude built it from the spec, and all twenty-nine checks passed.
The spec is one Markdown file. The data model, the rules, four phase prompts and all twenty-nine checks.
